chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Richard M. Jones and the New Orleans pianists who migrated to Chicago
summary: Danny and Milt recall Richard M. Jones, producer and writer, and the New Orleans migrants Clarence and Spencer Williams, Jelly Roll and the Hightowers.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Richard, but they called him Mynee(?) Jones. He was one of the pioneer producers of records, and writer, and he should have had his own publishing company. But them days it was... Handy just was about the only one, Handy and...
I don't want to ...(?)..., but I think he had kind of eyes for my Mom. He lived right across the hall from me. And that made him take an interest in me. He gave me my first harmony book, man.
Richard M. Jones. So go on. So he was the piano player in this group?
Yeah. Well, all of them migrated from New Orleans to Chicago. Clarence Williams, Spencer Williams,
Oh, Mr. Hightower. There was a couple of them, wasn't it?
Was there a couple of them Hightower brothers.
Yeah... Well, I knew of one. Him and his wife.
Right, that's right, his wife, Mrs. Hightower. They were very big in the union in Chicago, Local 208.
Yeah. They were pioneers in helping... getting into things.
